assertions.name: Crow amplification during approach is FINITE and power-law (A = (d0^2/V1_0)^(s*/3)); no finite-time linear 3D runaway before the overlap cutoff engages
assertions.source: log e-folds; exponent = s*/3 exactly; scope (a): Crow linear theory + phase-1 approach law, constant s*, alone

description: U3 (bean qou-7fi2): quantifies the named 3D escape of the two-regime pair model — the Crow instability — during the phase-1 approach. sigma = s* Gamma/(2 pi d^2) along d^2 = d0^2 - (Gamma/pi) t integrates to N_e = (s*/2) ln(d0^2/d^2_ov); with the strain-race overlap d^2_ov = d0^2 rho^(2/3) the amplification is the power law A = rho^(-s*/3) (~rho^-0.27 classically) — bounded for every finite core ratio, logarithmic e-folds, no linear finite-time runaway. Sweeps s* in {0.5, 0.8, 1.2} and rho in {1e-2..1e-8}; viscous-overlap engagement (pair_viscous_core_race) taken when earlier. Honest caveats: s* held constant (classically it depends on the evolving core/separation ratio); linear theory only (nonlinear saturation / reconnection not modeled); scope (a) throughout. The 2D reduction degrades only polynomially in the core ratio before the cutoff engages — the 3D escape requires large seed perturbations or the nonlinear regime, which remain the open content of qou-ohaz U3.
